question: Can the selected sources justify a learned controller for a vehicle whose configuration, operating conditions, safety criteria and validation data have not been supplied?

u199bc87ac63c4d9e8535.quote: Web world models increasingly predict the consequences of candidate actions before agents act, yet a plausible predicted future does not necessarily support the correct safety decision. In a matched human evaluation of 3,000 predictions from ten frozen open models, 86.1% are judged semantically plausible. However, several models exhibit highly asymmetric authorisation behaviour, combining low false-safe execution with poor recall of clarifiable ASK cases and a strong preference for BLOCK. This motivates safety sufficiency: whether a predictive interface preserves and exposes the policy-decisive information required to distinguish actions that may be EXECUTED, require clarification through ASK, or should be BLOCKED. We introduce SafeWebWorld, a benchmark for evaluating safety sufficiency across five web-safety domains through action-conditioned futures, policy-decisive evidence, and policy-conditioned decisions. Under a controlled Security-Aligned Supervised Fine-Tuning protocol, evidence preservation can improve substantially while authorisation-sensitive decisions deteriorate. To determine whether this deterioration reflects loss of authorisation-sensitive score structure or a failure of the decision readout, we introduce Latent Authorisation Recovery (LAR). Frozen-score recalibration reveals substantial but backbone-dependent recovery, while paired recovery provides only a modest additional gain. Yet within-family and matched-authorisation evaluations remain poor, showing that aggregate recoverability does not imply robust fine-grained authorisation behaviour.

ub314a0bb598e7e9dfabe.quote: Fairness benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) are overwhelmingly English-born and American in their social categories; translated versions carry those categories into societies where they do not apply, and almost none fix their hypotheses before the models are run. We present Qistas (Arabic qistas, "the just balance"), a protocol for evaluating how LLMs treat the social, confessional, and regional constituencies of a society, portable across countries and instantiated first for Iraq. In its pilot form it measures only what needs no verdict on contested truth: procedural symmetry across matched counterfactual pairs, differential refusal, stereotype reliance under ambiguity, and terminological framing of documented events. Every measurement is paired by construction and analysed with paired machinery (sign-flip permutation tests, exact McNemar tests, template-clustered bootstrap intervals, Holm-corrected families), with a power analysis that states, before any data exist, the smallest effect each axis can detect after the design effect of template clustering. We release the authoring apparatus (a pruned 3x5 taxonomy with four cells closed by design, per-type checklists, a cumulative rulings log, a structural audit, and a human review notebook) and report its first field test: a semantic review of a 58-item seed bank in which 24 of 25 template groups failed at least one check.

spans.text: Fairness benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) are overwhelmingly English-born and American in their social categories; translated versions carry those categories into societies where they do not apply, and almost none fix their hypotheses before the models are run. We present Qistas (Arabic qistas, "the just balance"), a protocol for evaluating how LLMs treat the social, confessional, and regional constituencies of a society, portable across countries and instantiated first for Iraq. In its pilot form it measures only what needs no verdict on contested truth: procedural symmetry across matched counterfactual pairs, differential refusal, stereotype reliance under ambiguity, and terminological framing of documented events. Every measurement is paired by construction and analysed with paired machinery (sign-flip permutation tests, exact McNemar tests, template-clustered bootstrap intervals, Holm-corrected families), with a power analysis that states, before any data exist, the smallest effect each axis can detect after the design effect of template clustering. We release the authoring apparatus (a pruned 3x5 taxonomy with four cells closed by design, per-type checklists, a cumulative rulings log, a structural audit, and a human review notebook) and report its first field test: a semantic review of a 58-item seed bank in which 24 of 25 template groups failed at least one check. The defect patterns it exposed (evaluation criteria leaking into prompts, token-level swaps that break Arabic agreement, epistemically unbalanced pairs, single-theme refusal probes, unwritten dialect twins counted as coverage) are, we argue, general hazards of counterfactual fairness benchmarks. This is a protocol paper, not a results paper: no model has been evaluated, and the accompanying pre-registration commits the hypotheses, metrics, exclusion rules, and analysis plan that the pilot will follow.

exact_initial_request_context.comparison_contract: Coverage is the single authoritative mapping. Do not emit comparison_claims or comparison_basis. An answer reference for a comparison must be an actual comparative finding with separately cited evidence handles from all necessary sources. Qualitative method contrasts require supported method descriptions, not necessarily common benchmarks. Empirical performance conclusions require compatible evaluation tasks, comparators, metric definitions and conditions. Source notes stay context if the requested comparison is unanswered; partial retains every gap and earns no full answer credit. Support, atomicity, qualifications and actual request relevance are checked independently.
exact_initial_request_context.coverage_wire_rule: Coverage alone maps sealed requested parts to emitted answer/context claim IDs. No claims.part_ids, missing/orphan/duplicate/overlapping references. Full abstention omits claims and ALL claim references. A comparison answer needs independently cited source bases; comparison-only notes leave the requested comparison unanswered.
exact_initial_request_context.identity_contract: Emit only actual claims in order. Server assigns c1,c2 and later positions. Coverage is the only answer/context mapping: exactly each required named part, all genuine gap reasons. Questions distinguish context_claim_ids (topic links, no factual premise) from premise_claim_ids (investigate_claim only, independently checked). The structural answer tag grants no full-answer credit.

procedural_rendering.rule: Neutral intents may have context_claim_ids but no premise_claim_ids. investigate_claim requires nonempty premise_claim_ids; never introduce an assertion outside the scored claims.

exact_initial_request_context.request_quality_rule: At most 12 atomic claims in research mode; about 500 characters per claim and 240 per explanation are SOFT targets only. Preserve qualifications rather than shortening into misleading claims. Record every requested part exactly once as answered, partial, lacks_evidence or omitted. Available but unreported information is omitted. Context notes do not answer a comparison. All semantic quality and factual prose remain reviewed. Partial requires useful answer refs AND genuine remaining gaps; answered requires no remaining gap. Context alone never earns answer credit.
